channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
item.description: Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.

item.title: Trump administration requests $50B in funding after nationwide flight disruptions
item.description: As air travel begins to return to normal following a Friday ground stop and weekend chaos, the battle now turns to Congress and a funding fight for the FAA.

item.title: Regulating AI will being a top priority for congressional Democrats in the new year
item.description: A big priority for the incoming Congress will be regulating artificial intelligence. Democrats will face stiff opposition from the Trump administration and its hands-off policy towards AI.

item.title: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss
item.description: Sleep can have a powerful impact on weight. Research shows it can affect appetite. There is also a two-way relationship between sleep quality and diet.

item.title: Affordability was a key issue for midterm voters. It helped make childcare one, too
item.description: Childcare costs have surged, putting a major financial burden on U.S. families. Advocates say the subject once on the fringes of political debate became a major issue during the midterms.
